name: [GPF97] c01
description: A Cepheid in the galaxy M95 that pulsates every 43.0 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 42.95 d in Kanbur et al. (2003), A&A 411, 361, VizieR J/A+A/411/361/table1 Galaxy = NGC3351, Cepheid = C1 (log(P) 1.633); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 42.95 d in Kanbur et al. (2003), A&A 411, 361, VizieR J/A+A/411/361/table1 Galaxy = NGC3351, Cepheid = C1 (log(P) 1.633); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M95, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2022ApJS..261...21Y; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in M95 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 9,951,724 pc (src/objects/m95-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 9,954,054 pc, inclination 41 deg, line of nodes 192 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Tully2009AJ....138..323T: The Extragalactic Distance Database (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009AJ....138..323T); catalogue reference Tully2009AJ....138..323T: 9954054.17352 pc (-136574.74332/+138474.687247); trgb

position.credit: Kanbur et al. (2003), A&A 411, 361, VizieR J/A+A/411/361/table1 Galaxy = NGC3351, Cepheid = C1, names the star in SIMBAD (SName); SIMBAD holds its position and names no paper for it

text.card: A Cepheid in the galaxy M95, 10.0 million parsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 43.0 days.
text.introduction: Kanbur et al. (2003) list its pulsation at 43.0 days.
text.locator: VizieR J/A+A/411/361/table1 Galaxy = NGC3351, Cepheid = C1: log(P)

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M95 is not measured
